samples.notes: The same sample appears in convention abstract R0660 (JPA 2024), which reports the same counts (176/439 = 40%). R0660 calls the participants 'general adults' (一般成人), but they are university students. The cut-off is described as 'exceeding' 14 points, so it is unclear whether the rule was >=14 or >14. Tada et al. 2022 is cited only as the source of the Japanese MQ; the text does not describe a validation. Co-occurrence with hyperacusis (HQ>=40 and MQ symptom>=14) was 32/439 = 7.3% (7.2% in the abstract); this is not extracted as a misophonia estimate. No sex-specific prevalence is reported, only mean scores by sex (Table 3). The study's meta-analysis of mean MQ scores includes other studies' samples, which are not extracted here.

codes.consistency_notes: Text and tables agree: Table 4 healthy 41/8/1 matches the text '16% (n=8)... 2% (n=1)'. Anxiety 31/25 of 121, depression 4/13 of 41 and OCD 8/4 of 29 match the text percentages. Table 4 column percentages use only the four listed diagnoses as the base (e.g., 8/51 = 15.7%), not the full groups. The 105 participants who chose 'misophonia' on the Sound Disturbance Problems Form equal the 56 disorder-level + 49 symptom-level cases. Text says 'major depressive disorder'; Table 2 says 'Depressive Disorder'. In the Discussion, OCPD '2.4% (n=6) of all participants' would be 6/263 = 2.3%. Table 1 gives age and sex only for all 263 participants by misophonia status, so these values cannot be given for each sample.
codes.note: The study has two samples recruited separately: 213 first-time psychiatric outpatients and 50 healthy volunteers (hospital staff and relatives). Authors report only combined estimates (263 participants: 56 disorder-level, 21.3%; 105 any misophonia, 39.9%), so the patient counts come from subtracting the healthy group in Tables 2 and 4. Level decisions for a reviewer to check: (1) Disorder-level is coded L2, not L3, because the Öz criteria were applied to forms the participants filled out themselves, and the text never says a clinician or trained interviewer applied them. (2) 'Any misophonia' combines self-identification with at least one trigger sound rated moderate, so it is coded L1 under rule G4. Symptom-level alone is a single, non-cumulative band and is not reported.

codes.excluded_samples: None excluded under E1: neither sample was recruited for misophonia. The 'S1 positive' and 'Clinical misophonia' columns in Table 3 are subsets of the two samples, not separate samples. The 32 self-reported autistic Prolific participants are a subgroup of the Prolific sample (extracted as a subgroup estimate).
codes.consistency_notes: 1) SPARK S1-positive count: Table 3 gives 647, but the text gives 645 ('Prolific: n = 833; SPARK: n = 645 affirmatively answered ... and went on to complete the full measure'; the IRT n is also 645). I used the table value (647). R0652 Table 1 gives 69.1% screening positive, and 69.1% x 936 = 647. The clinical count of 332 is given over all 936, so G10 is satisfied. 2) SPARK participant flow differs between reports: R0998 gives 1271 consented, 1121 completed the measures and 185 excluded, leaving 936. R0440 gives 'the original sample of 1178 individuals with sufficient data on all DST measures' reduced to 936. R0652 lists exclusions of 134+45+34+3+23 (categories may overlap) plus 108 dropouts. 3) The prevalence counts agree across R0998, R0652 and R0440 (332/936 = 35.5%; female 44.2%, male 20.5%). R0652 adds a sex-weighted 29.1%. 4) Prolific: 102/1403 = 7.27% and 144/1403 = 10.26%, matching the text. Table 3 female 74/717 and male 28/686 are consistent with the 72.5% female share among cases. 5) Prolific age maximum is inferred: the combined range is 18–83, and R0652 gives a SPARK maximum of 80. 6) In R0998 Table 3, the SPARK gender rows sum to 781, not 936 (gender data probably missing for some); this does not affect the estimates. 7) The previous-diagnosis cross-tab (Prolific 7/2/1; SPARK 19/1/1) matches '29 of 31' in the Discussion.
codes.note: Both samples use the DVMSQ algorithm, which this report develops. The algorithm is criterion-based (adapted from the Revised Amsterdam Criteria and the consensus definition) but has no interview or ROC anchoring, so JBI 6 = no. Topic disclosure is coded 'no' for both samples because the adverts said 'sensory sensitivities', not sounds; a reviewer may judge this borderline. The SPARK sex-weighted 29.1% (R0652) is entered as weighted_pct, but it is a post-stratification to an assumed 3:1 male:female ratio, not a set of design weights.
